s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty with mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma
Anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements
Low serum zinc level
Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands on biopsy
Negative direct immunofluorescence test
Negative Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab

differentials: Chronic lymphocytic inflammation with pontine atrophy
per_call: Chronic lymphocytic inflammation with pontine atrophy

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and association with multiple myeloma

shortlist.label: Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Association with multiple myeloma and presence of systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and presence of skin lesions

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and presence of skin lesions

shortlist.label: Acquired zinc deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Low serum zinc level and presence of skin lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of subepidermal blisters with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining is highly suggestive of amyloidosis, particularly in the context of a patient with a history of multiple myeloma, which is a known association with amyloidosis.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: Negative direct immunofluorescence test and lack of specific autoantibodies make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: Typically presents with tense bullae and linear IgG and C3 deposition on direct immunofluorescence, which is not seen in this case

rejected.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
rejected.why: Characterized by the presence of autoantibodies against type VII collagen, which is not mentioned in the case, and typically presents with trauma-induced blisters

rejected.label: Acquired zinc deficiency
rejected.why: While the patient has a low serum zinc level, the skin findings and biopsy results are more suggestive of amyloidosis than a simple zinc deficiency
